title: The Wisdom of Solomon and the Vineyard

full_text:
Two men appeared before King David in Jerusalem to settle a bitter dispute. The first was an honest farmer whose lush vineyard was heavy with ripening purple grapes; the second was a shepherd whose flock of sheep had broken into the vineyard at night, trampling the vines and devouring the entire crop.

King David, hearing that the damage equaled the value of the sheep, judged according to strict law: 'Let the flock of sheep be forfeited and given to the vineyard owner to compensate for his lost harvest.'

Young Solomon, who sat beside the throne, bowed respectfully and said: 'O father, with your royal leave, may I suggest a judgment that contains both justice and mercy?'

David smiled: 'Speak, Solomon.'

Solomon said: 'Let the vineyard owner take the sheep for one year: he shall enjoy their milk, their wool, and their newborn lambs to nourish his family. Meanwhile, let the shepherd take the ruined vineyard: he shall water the soil, prune the vines, and cultivate the land with his own labor until the vines bear purple grapes once more!

At the end of the year, let the vineyard be returned to the farmer, and let the flock of sheep be returned to the shepherd!'

King David marveled at his son’s profound equity: 'Your judgment is greater than mine, Solomon! Strict law merely transfers property, but your wisdom restores the loss while teaching the offender to repair his wrong with honest labor.'

The two men embraced with joyful gratitude, and the judgment of Solomon became an eternal model of restorative justice across all nations.
moral: True justice repairs the injury of the victim while preserving the livelihood of the offender.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Story of David and Solomon"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
